_README: Signature registry for the Marg Report Router. ADDING A NEW REPORT TYPE IS A
DATA EDIT HERE -- no code change. Run 'marg_router.py --learn <file>' on a
sample and it prints a ready-to-paste block.
Matching rule: title_regex AND header must BOTH match, else the file is
refused (a partial match is never parsed). Unknown files are quarantined,
type          short code, becomes the archive folder name
variant       distinguishes layouts of the same report (DETAIL vs SUMMARY1)
title_regex   matched against the title row (case-insensitive)
header        expected column headers, in order; matched as a prefix
uploadable    true = a VERIFIED file is copied to the Outbox for sending
end_marker    optional text that must appear near the end (completeness)

signatures._comment: S205: the SUPPLIER/ITEM WISE purchase statement -- a THIRD purchase report, and the richest. PURCHASE_BILLWISE gives bill -> supplier -> date -> amount; PURCHASE_SUPPLIERWISE gives the supplier view; this gives the LINES INSIDE each bill, with batch, expiry, rate, discount and net rate. The three join on BILL. This is the Purchase Portal's (D335) real input.
signatures.end_marker_note: S205: MEASURED against all five real exports, not copied from the sibling signature. "GRAND TOTAL" -- which PURCHASE_SUPPLIERWISE uses -- matches 0 of 5 here, because in THIS layout Marg splits it across two cells ('GRAND' | 'TOTAL') and ends_with() searches cells, not rows. Copying it would have refused every real report. 'Digital Purchase' is Marg's own footer, the literal last line, so it is a true completeness signal; 'GRAND' also matches 5/5 but appears inside item descriptions in Indian pharma catalogues and would risk a FALSE GREEN on a truncated export. If Marg ever stops printing the footer these reports go to _REFUSED with the reason stated -- visible and recoverable by a rescan, which is the safe direction to be wrong in.

signatures._note: S219 M2. Item-level purchase rows grouped BY BILL. Same column layout as PURCHASE_ITEMWISE (grouped by supplier) - kept as its own type so one folder never mixes two groupings of the same rows. end_marker derived from the sample itself: the sibling's 'Digital Purchase' is ABSENT here (Marg rotates its footer advert), and copying it would refuse every export as TRUNCATED - the S205 failure. uploadable stays false ON PURPOSE: the VPS has no purchase tables until M3, and false is recorded here loudly because 'uploadable: false' is the quietest way for a feed not to exist (S212).

signatures._note: S219 M2. Marg's own credit-note register. Derived from ONE sample (Aug full month); if a later export merges its columns differently the router REFUSES loudly rather than parsing a guess, which is the designed failure. uploadable false until the returns build (M7) has somewhere to put it.

S224. The SAME 'SALE RETURN FROM .. TO ..' title emitted as a 4-column bill-list (bill, date, party, amount) instead of the DEFAULT credit-note register. Two real exports (01-Apr..02-Sep-2026, 197 credit notes, cell-for-cell identical) were REFUSED as 'title matches SALE_RETURN but the column layout does not'. Same type, own variant: one figure per credit note, no tax/discount split, so it can never stand in for DEFAULT. end_marker derived from the file itself: Marg prints this layout's total row as the spaced word 'T o t a l' (the sibling's 'TOTAL' matches 0 of 2 real exports - the S205 trap again). LIMIT, stated: the same label heads every page's running total, so ends_with() (last 40 rows) catches a cut only when it falls 40+ rows after the previous page total; a cut early in a page passes as complete. The final grand total equals the sum of every dated row, which is the check a reader should make. The DATE sits in column 2 and the router reads body dates from column 1 only, so data_from/data_to stay blank and the row is dated by its title - stated so nobody reads blank data dates as an empty report. uploadable false, like DEFAULT: the VPS has no returns table (M7); nothing is sent.
